summary: Iteration 14 — Recipe Card PDF validation bug verified end-to-end. Backend pytest test_recipe_card.py: 6/6 PASS (upload rejects stub/text/empty → 422; valid one-page PDF upload+attach+download returns 200 %PDF with attachment disposition; legacy stub in storage → GET card returns 422 'valid PDF'; missing storage object → 404; auth matrix 401/402/200; live Rainbow Fruit Kabobs (Copy) id a3f29d4d... GET card returns 422). Frontend UI: on the actual Kabobs (Copy) recipe page as admin, click Download Recipe Card → NO new tab opened, sonner toast "This recipe card isn't a valid PDF yet. Please check back soon." shown, button briefly says Preparing… then returns to Download Recipe Card. Route-intercept mocks: 402 → 'Recipe cards are for active members...' toast; 404 → "This recipe card isn't available right now." toast; 200 with body 'not a pdf' → client-side %PDF header check fires the same 'valid PDF' toast. Admin Recipes tab upload via [data-testid=admin-recipe-card] with the 45-byte stub → toast 'Recipe card must be a valid PDF with at least one page' (surfacing server 422 detail). Regression: recipe page h1 renders title, weekly-drop 'Send preview to me' button present in admin Recipes tab, Flags tab still shows 'Email: Resend' indicator. Kabobs recipe records untouched, no emails triggered.

fix_applied_by_tester.issue: Duplicate `const [cardBusy, setCardBusy] = useState(false);` declaration on lines 12 and 13 caused webpack Syntax error 'Identifier cardBusy has already been declared (13:9)'. The ENTIRE frontend was failing to compile — every route would have been broken for users. Removed the duplicate line; webpack now compiles cleanly (1 warning, 0 errors). Root cause: likely a bad merge / edit that pasted the useState line twice when adding the busy state.
fix_applied_by_tester.impact_if_not_fixed: Frontend totally down; no recipe page (or any page) would render for anyone.

action_items: Main agent: acknowledge the duplicate-useState fix in Recipe.jsx. Ensure your local edits don't reintroduce it. Consider adding an ESLint 'no-redeclare' rule or a pre-commit check — this was a build-breaker that shipped in the last patch.

Minor code review nit: Recipe.jsx effect depends on [id, kitchen] but the wake-lock branch inside the effect only makes sense when kitchen is true; fine as-is but grouping in a separate effect would be cleaner.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _pdf_page_count/upload/get_recipe_card path is solid: rejects stub PDFs at both upload (422) and download (422) time, and the auth ordering 401→402→404→422 matches the frontend's toast copy exactly.

Recipe.jsx downloadCard() does a defensive client-side %PDF-header check on the blob — good belt-and-suspenders in case a proxy strips the 422 or a legacy stub sneaks through. Consider also verifying blob.type startsWith 'application/pdf' before creating the object URL.
Admin.jsx uploadFile toast surfaces err.response.data.detail — good; keep this pattern for all upload variants.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (7/7 scenarios: happy path, 3 mocked error codes, admin upload rejection, 2 regression checks)

rca of the issue: REPORTED BUG (recipe card download opens a broken browser PDF viewer): backend fix (_pdf_page_count + upload/download validation) is correct and tests all pass. However a second, unshipped-but-critical bug was introduced in the same patch — /app/frontend/src/pages/Recipe.jsx contained the line `const [cardBusy, setCardBusy] = useState(false);` twice back-to-back (lines 12 & 13).
